summary: Silent tenant heartbeat gap causing GPU hoarding and stalled batching in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports sustained p50/p99 latency increase and drop in overall throughput for their pinned routes on a dedicated GPU pool. Symptoms started ~2026-03-11 07:20 PDT and persisted intermittently across the 3-hour window.

Impact:
- ForgeAI observed 35% drop in generated tokens/minute and p99 latency regression from 220ms -> 780ms for batched routes.
- No user-visible 5xx errors, but increased queueing and longer batch head-of-line times caused timeouts at application layer.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-west-3 (us-west).
- Customer uses reserved capacity with pinned model versions (gpt-open-13b-q4).
- Autoscaler configured with predictive shrink enabled and aggressive pod consolidation window (5m).

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) ForgeAI sends steady workload of small short-stream requests (avg 150 tokens) starting ~07:00.
2) Around 07:20 autoscaler began a predictive shrink cycle. Several GPU leases were retired.
3) At ~07:22 serving logs show a subset of tenant allocations stopped renewing heartbeats for ~12-18s (no explicit error).
4) Scheduler treated the stale leases as live and left slot assignments in limbo while balancer attempted a partial rebalance -> resulted in ephemeral "hoarded" slots where GPU threads were pinned but not accepting new batches.
5) Batchers reported head-of-line delays; KV cache pins prevented reuse of existing session state, forcing repeated cold KV loads.

Logs / traces (snippets):
- scheduler: lease_refresh delta=18s tenant=forgeai-tenant-42 slot_id=gp0-17 status=heartbeat-missed
- batcher: blocked_queue_len=43 head_of_line_wait_ms=1200 slot_owner=gp0-17
- runtime: small_stream_ctx_swap=3 repeated_kv_fetch=7 slot_state=allocated_but_idle

Temporary mitigations attempted:
- Support manually bumped the predictive shrink window to 15m for the affected pool (reduced rebalance frequency).
- We forced a graceful drain of the two most-impacted GPUs which temporarily freed slots and restored throughput to ~90% baseline.

Next steps / plan:
- SRE to instrument heartbeat jitter metrics and correlate with autoscaler actions (ETA 2026-03-14).
- Engineering to add defensive check: treat heartbeat gap >8s as explicit preemption event to avoid leaving slots pinned during rebalance (investigation PR planned).
- Recommend customer temporarily disable predictive shrink for critical windows until fix (reached out via support).

Follow-ups required:
- Post-incident runbook update to include heartbeat-gap handling and recommended autoscale tuning for short-stream heavy tenants.
- Evaluate KV cache eviction policy under slot churn to avoid repeated cold loads.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: autoscaler-triggered rebalance overlapping with transient heartbeat jitter caused scheduler to leave allocated slot state inconsistent. Evidence: cluster events show shrink step at 07:21, followed by heartbeat gaps from multiple allocations belonging to the same tenant. Stack traces show batchers waiting on slot_owner threads that did not accept batches. Alternative hypothesis: tenant side created many short-lived streams that saturated slot-owner thread pools leading to missed heartbeat renewals. Correlation found between small-stream rate spike (ForgeAI traffic) and heartbeat-missed events.

Key dashboards inspected:
- Grafana: dashboards/cluster/dedicated-pools/dp-west-3 (p99 latency, allocation churn)
- Tracing: jaeger/trace/forgeai-requests (span shows long batcher wait)

Evidence artifacts:
- scheduler-event-log: https://logs.redwood.ai/dp-west-3/2026-03-11/scheduler.gz
- grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/dp-west-3/overview?from=2026-03-11T07:00&to=2026-03-11T10:00

Workaround effectiveness: manual drain restored throughput temporarily; however, underlying race remains. Changes to autoscaler tuning reduce incidence but do not eliminate heartbeat jitter.
comments: 2026-03-11 08:05 - Support (Aisha R. Patel): Notified ForgeAI of ongoing investigation and recommended disabling predictive shrink as an interim. Customer agreed and paused predictive shrink at 08:12.

2026-03-11 09:00 - SRE (Diego Mendez): Performed controlled drain on gp0-17 and gp0-18, observed immediate recovery in batch acceptance. Collected heap/dump from slot threads and forwarded to runtime team.

2026-03-11 10:22 - Runtime Eng (Lin Zhao): Initial analysis of dumps indicates slot-owner threads entered a spin-wait state while performing repeated KV fetches; likely backpressure from remote storage causing missed heartbeat renews.
2026-03-12 11:15 - Support (Aisha): Customer reports improved stability after disablement; asks for ETA on permanent fix and runbook updates.
2026-03-13 14:02 - SRE (Diego): Creating follow-up INT ticket to track autoscaler defensive behavior change and runbook update. See INT-74921 for internal tracking.
private_notes: Engineering to prototype quick fix: mark slot as preempted if heartbeat gap >8s and trigger an immediate lightweight reassign to avoid hoarding. If that change is risky, fallback to conservative autoscaler parameters and improved telemetry. Plan for small canary rollout in dp-west-3 after unit tests.
